items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: See, Mr. Bubbles -- Buck and Bubbles, one time when the Jimmy Lunceford Orchestra came up to New York City... And it gave Mr. Lunceford an idea, I'm quite sure, because the next thing that I know of... they had a record on the juke boxes by Jimmy Lunceford and Orchestra

ctx.x: -- more advanced, and you had already learned the other forms of tap, and up to that point they were sort of novelty sort of forms. But now you felt as if you had -- you were starting to -- your mind was starting to think in terms of more complex sort of rhythms.

Yes. See, Mr. Bubbles -- Buck and Bubbles, one time when the Jimmy Lunceford Orchestra came up to New York City, and they were all in a show one time up there, and Buck and Bubbles I would say was always stopping the show. And they'd have to do these encores. But the people loved to hear Bubbles tap dance, you know. He got a taste of what happened to me down south. They'd say, "Dance, Bubbles, Dance," and they called his name and everything. And he would say something funny about his partner had run out of music…

that? What instrument are you going to play?" He'd say, "I'm standing on my instrument," you see, or something like that, and make people laugh. So he says, "All right," he says, "I'll play my instrument and you repeat after me, you try to repeat after me." So he would do a step, some kind of rhythm, you know. Then one of the guys, he'd look at him, you, you. "Well, which one of you? You heard it didn't you?" And the guy would jump up with his instrument and try to play what he heard, you see. And he would choose…
